articles.title: Arizona DACA Renewals Now Take Five to Six Months as Delays Cost Jobs and Licences
articles.excerpt: Arizona advocates say renewal waits have stretched from about two months to five or six months under new USCIS screening and biometrics requirements. CBS News reports the national backlog of pending renewals has passed 125,000.
articles.image_caption: A USCIS I-797 Notice of Action for Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA). Arizona DACA renewals now take five to six months, costing recipients jobs and licences.
articles.nri_angle: Arizona is home to 16,000-20,000 DACA recipients; when a renewal lapses, work authorization and driver licences lapse with it, and advocates say calls for help now arrive daily.

articles.title: DHS Makes End of 540-Day Work Permit Extension Permanent in Final Rule
articles.excerpt: The Department of Homeland Security's final rule, effective on Federal Register publication on October 14, means most EAD renewals filed on or after October 30, 2025 no longer extend work authorization while they are pending — a direct hit for H-4 spouses and asylum applicants.
articles.image_caption: The US Department of Homeland Security headquarters in Washington, DC. DHS made the end of the 540-day work permit extension permanent in a final rule.
articles.nri_angle: H-4 spouses of H-1B workers — most of them Indian women — lose the safety net that kept them employed while USCIS processed renewals; a pending renewal no longer extends the card past its printed expiry date.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: DHS Proposes Ending Deference to Prior H-1B and L-1 Petition Approvals
articles.excerpt: A proposed rule would remove the requirement that USCIS defer to earlier I-129 approvals, exposing H-1B and L-1 extensions and amendments to fresh adjudication, more evidence requests, and higher denial risk.
articles.image_caption: The US Department of Homeland Security headquarters in Washington, DC. DHS has proposed ending automatic deference to prior H-1B and L-1 petition approvals.
articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals are a large share of H-1B holders and file repeated extensions while awaiting green cards, so losing deference to prior approvals would make renewals less predictable for workers and employers.

articles.title: Federal Agents Search Ilhan Omar's Washington Home Under Court-Authorized Warrant

articles.title: Federal Court Postpones Rule Ending Duration of Status for Student Visas
articles.excerpt: A federal judge in Massachusetts issued a nationwide injunction one day before a DHS rule was set to replace open-ended duration-of-status admissions with four-year caps for F and J visa holders — keeping the old system alive while the government appeals.
articles.image_caption: Students on a US university campus. A federal court has postponed a rule ending duration of status for student visas.
articles.nri_angle: Roughly 352,000 Indian students — the largest international-student cohort in the U.S. — are directly affected: the blocked rule's four-year cap and discretionary extension process would have hit Indian PhD and STEM OPT students hardest.

articles.title: Microsoft Disputes Vance's 'Foreign Indentured Servants' Claim With Its Own H-1B Data
articles.excerpt: In a Thursday-afternoon statement, the company said 80% of its H-1B filings last year were extensions for existing employees, not new hires; Vance says the fraud task force has opened multiple criminal investigations.
articles.image_caption: US Vice President JD Vance, whose claim that H-1B workers are 'foreign indentured servants' Microsoft disputed with its own H-1B hiring data.
articles.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of Indian H-1B professionals at the eight named firms face frozen PERM applications, the critical bridge to green cards; Microsoft's rebuttal and the criminal investigations will decide whether the freeze holds.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
